title: Botvinnik against Capablanca, 1938: a pawn storm cashed in by two sacrifices
outcomes: Tries each of five key moments before seeing the move and compares the attempt with the engine's first choice
Names which core idea (deflection or removing the defender) 30.Ba3 and 31.Nh5+ use
Says what the engine's rating before 26.Re6 does and does not show about when the game was decided

steps.text: **Botvinnik (White) against Capablanca (Black)**, round 11 of the AVRO tournament, Rotterdam, 22 November 1938; a Nimzo-Indian Defense that White won. You play White at five moments, before you see the move, and compare your choice with the engine's first choice and with the game. Engine ratings are evidence at a stated depth, not proof. Whether it is a great game is opinion; the moves are facts.

steps.caption: Moves 1 to 17. Step through them; the first decision comes at the end.

line.say: Black plays the Nimzo-Indian Defense with Bb4.
Black's bishop took the knight on c3 and White recaptured with the b-pawn.
White tucks the king away with Ne2 and castling.
The knight goes to a5 and White is to move: your first decision is next.

claims.statement: After 17...Na5 a black knight stands on a5.

steps.caption: Moves 18 to 23. Step through them; the second decision comes at the end.

line.say: Black's knight goes to b3.
White pushed the e-pawn; Black takes the pawn on a4 with the queen.
Black pushes f5 beside White's pawn on e5.
White takes en passant: the e5 pawn captures on f6.
The knight recaptures. White to move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine rates the position before 18.f3 at least one pawn better for White.

steps.caption: Moves 24 and 25. The third decision comes next.

line.say: The pawn goes to f5, attacking the pawn on g6.
Black trades rooks on e1.
White recaptures with the other rook.
Black puts the second rook on the e-file.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine rates the position before 24.f5 at least one pawn better for White.

steps.caption: Moves 26 to 29. The fourth decision comes next.

line.say: The rook goes to e6, where Black's rook can take it.
Black takes the rook.
The f-pawn recaptures and now stands on e6.
The queen goes to f4.
White's queen centralizes on e5; Black's queen goes to e7.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine rates the position before 26.Re6 at least two pawns better for White.
After 26.Re6 Rxe6 27.fxe6 a white pawn stands on e6.

steps.caption: Move 30. Black could decline the bishop, but the game continued with Qxa3. The fifth decision comes next.

line.say: The bishop goes to a3, attacking the queen on e7.
Black takes the bishop with the queen. White to move.

claims.statement: Before 30.Ba3 two black pieces defend the knight on f6 (the queen and the king).
After 30.Ba3 Qxa3 only one black piece defends the knight on f6 (the king).

steps.caption: Moves 31 to 41, the end of the record. The engine finds other Black replies to 31.Nh5+, but they are not shown.

line.say: The knight gives check on h5.
Black takes the knight with the g-pawn.
The queen gives check on the open g-file.
The queen takes the knight on f6 with check.
The e-pawn goes to e7, close to promoting.
Black checks again; the king steps out of it.
The king takes the pawn on h5.
The record ends here with 1-0 for White.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine rates the position before 31.Nh5+ at least four pawns better for White.

steps.text: **Core skills used, not re-taught.** *Deflection* (30.Ba3): after the queen takes the bishop, only the king still defends the knight on f6. *Deflection again* (31.Nh5+): the g-pawn takes the knight and leaves the g-file, so the queen checks on g5. *Loose piece*: the check drives the king to f8, where it no longer guards f6, and Qxf6+ wins the knight. Where was it decided? At depth 16 the engine already rated the position before 26.Re6 at least two pawns better: the finish cashed in an earlier gain.

steps.prompt: Which of the five moments (18.f3, 24.f5, 26.Re6, 30.Ba3, 31.Nh5+) would you have missed in a game of your own, and what would you have had to notice to find it?
